reason: The text is fundamentally theocentric and emphasizes religious/cosmic conflict far more than political struggle. The passage centers on God's divine power and miraculous intervention (God as 'a man of war,' parting the waters, destroying Pharaoh's army through divine action) rather than on the Hebrews' own political agency or struggle for liberty. The deliverance is presented exclusively as God's salvific act (ישועה - divine salvation) within a covenant relationship, with repeated declarations of God's eternal sovereignty (יְהוָה יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד - 'The Lord shall reign forever'). The Hebrews appear as passive recipients of divine redemption rather than active agents in a political liberation struggle.
